title: Fractal basin geometry and the limits to predictability and reproducibility in deep learning
abstract: arXiv:2510.05606v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Fundamental limits to predictability are central to our understanding of many physical and computational systems. In deep learning, training outcomes are notoriously difficult to predict and reproduce, yet the mechanism underlying these difficulties has remained unclear. Here we propose fractal, riddled basin geometry as a unifying dynamical-systems mechanism: every initialization leading to one solution lies arbitrarily close to initializations leading to different solutions, forming a fat fractal with structure at arbitrarily fine scales. Using a minimal neural network model, we analytically establish the classical route to riddling and derive a near-zero uncertainty exponent: even sharp increases in initialization precision yield only marginal gains in outcome predictability. In deep networks, intertwined training destinations and near-zero parameter-space exponents provide robust signatures consistent with riddling across tested

translated_title: 分形吸引盆几何与深度学习中可预测性和可复现性的极限
translated_abstract: 可预测性的基本极限是我们理解许多物理和计算系统的核心。在深度学习中，训练结果以难以预测和复现而著称，然而这些困难背后的机制一直不明确。在这里，我们提出分形的、相互穿透的吸引盆几何作为统一的动力系统机制：每一个导向某一解的初始化都任意接近于导向不同解的初始化，从而形成一个在任意精细尺度上都具有结构的胖分形。利用一个最小化的神经网络模型，我们解析地建立了通往穿透现象的经典路径，并推导出接近于零的不确定性指数：即使初始化精度急剧提高，也只能带来结果可预测性的微小提升。在深度网络中，相互交织的训练终点和接近零的参数空间指数提供了与穿透现象一致的稳健特征标志。
tldr: 深度学习训练结果难以预测和复现的根本原因在于损失景观中分形且相互穿透的吸引盆几何结构——即使大幅提高初始化精度，结果的可预测性也几乎不会改善。
en_tdlr: The unpredictability and irreproducibility of deep learning training arise from fractal, riddled basin geometry in the loss landscape, where even sharp increases in initialization precision yield only marginal gains in outcome predictability.
